# Rendering and teardown

- **Fog coverage**: `fog/fogCoverage.ts` replays saved paint and erase operations into bounded eighth-pixel shapes. `lighting/polygonClip.ts` owns the only clipping-library import. `FogOfWarRenderer` owns one map-aware `FogCoverageCache`, shared with `FogCanvasCompositor` and visibility consumers through `getCommittedCoverage()`. Immutable record identity avoids repeated geometry work; a single appended operation can reuse the previous shape, while observed undo/redo snapshots replay. Every lookup checks map identity, so an earlier subscriber can safely read the new map before the renderer clears its old pixels. The compositor draws committed rings with NonZero winding and keeps temporary strokes separate. Invalid committed geometry produces an opaque picture and excludes player tokens and door badges until valid data arrives. Per-operation sprites remain invisible editing helpers.
- **Fog and visible tokens**: `PlayerSightTokens` composes committed fog with lighting for player captures, session view and existing peek. Fog tests the displayed sprite centre (the stored position before a sprite exists), including on unlit scenes and when the lighting controller is absent. Covered tokens lose their art, labels, bars, conditions, sensed outlines and drag rulers. Fog also hides held tokens without ending their captured drag; the held exception applies only to lighting. Membership is cached by displayed object, coverage identity and both coordinates; movement updates only that token's outline. Door badges and their player hit targets require current sight and an uncovered midpoint; unlit scenes still show no player door badges. Fog presentation never changes sight sources, explored memory or the normal GM view.
- **Render on change**: `src/app/pixi/RenderScheduler.ts` replaces the Application's per-tick render. It renders only when PIXI's render groups hold pending changes (moved, added, removed or hidden children; updated Graphics, Sprites or Text). Ticker callbacks still run every frame. Anything PIXI cannot see must call `requestRender(app)`: pixels uploaded into an existing texture (`source.update()`), hand-animated filter properties, renderer settings, off-screen renders that consume pending updates (`generateTexture`).
- **Destroy with `destroyTree`** (`src/app/pixi/utils/destroyTree.ts`): in PIXI 8 `destroy({ children: true })` keeps every Graphics' geometry registered with the renderer until the app is destroyed. Never detach a display object with `removeChild` alone when it is not reused.
- **Vault images reach PIXI as bytes**: read with `vault.readBinary` and decoded by `decodeImage` (`pixi/decodedImage.ts`: `createImageBitmap`, or an `<img>` drawn on a canvas for SVG), and by `TextureCache` for token art; map backgrounds go to the tile worker as bytes (Map images, below). Never hand a file's resource URL (`getResourcePath`) to `Assets.load`: PIXI fetches it, and Obsidian answers a `fetch` of `app://` only where its installer registered the scheme for the Fetch API (since installer 1.4.5) and for cross-origin requests (since 1.13, which Electron 40 and later demand). On an older installer, or one run on a newer Electron than it came with, every scene failed with "Failed to fetch" while `<img>` and the vault still showed the file. `tests/gpu/mapBackgroundLoad.gpu.test.ts` opens a scene where the URL cannot be fetched.
- **Rebuild only what changed**: store-driven renderers compare the new record with the previous one (Immer keeps unchanged references) and move objects in place instead of recreating them on every update, e.g. during drags.
- **Token UI sizing** (`src/app/pixi/token-renderer/tokenSizing.ts`): all token UI lives in world space in anchor containers on the token's edge, laid out in UI units (1 = a medium token on a 70px grid). Resize and rotate handles scale with the token via `tokenUIScale(spriteSize)`, like Owlbear Rodeo, and don't turn with it (resize left/right, rotate at the top). Resource bars, nameplates and condition markers (`TokenUIRenderer`) do not follow the token's size: they rest at `restingTokenUIScale(gridSize)` while unselected or dragged, and a selected token's grow to `selectedTokenUIScale`, a constant screen size like map pins (recomputed on viewport zoom). The +/- controls take the bars' scale through `UIManager`. `InteractionController` reports held tokens, so a press that selects a token and a drag keep its bars at rest until release. Canvas animations use `ValueTransition` (`src/app/pixi/utils/ValueTransition.ts`) with the motion tokens from `src/app/utils/motion.ts`.
- **Player window**: the players' picture is rendered for the player window, not copied from the GM's pane. *What it shows* (`playerFrame`, `services/playerFrame.ts`, pure): the frame is centred on the centre of the GM's view and scaled so that everything the GM's view shows fits into the window (`scale = min(w / view.width, h / view.height)`, in the window's points), and the rest of the window shows the map around it. So players never see less than the GM, may see map beside the GM's pane (a room is hidden from them by fog or lighting, never by scrolling it off the GM's screen), and a sidebar that makes the pane narrower changes nothing for them where the pane's height decides the fit. That is also all they can see: the frame is the smallest rectangle of the window's shape around the view, never more, a smaller pane never shows them more, and a view that cannot be read (no viewport yet, a pane, zoom or centre that is no positive finite number, or sides so small that the frame's own scale would be none) gives no frame at all (`viewOf` and `playerFrame` return null, and the mirror keeps the last frame): there is no default view and no fallback to the whole map. `PixiAppManager.resize` keeps the view's centre when the pane changes size (and emits `moved`), so the frame does not slide either; a pane another Obsidian tab covers is `display: none` and measures 0 × 0, which `resize` never takes, since the viewport would take it and the GM's view would have no size. *Its pixels*: the window's own device pixels (`PlayerWindowService.windowScreen`: the canvas fills the window; the mirror compares it on every display frame, so a resized window or one moved to a screen with another pixel ratio is stale), up to `PLAYER_FRAME_PIXEL_BUDGET` (2560 × 1440; a larger window gets a frame of its shape with that many pixels, which CSS scales up smoothly, and never fewer pixels than the pane has); a 3840 × 2160 frame took four to eight times the old capture, half of it bringing the pixels across. It is multisampled below two pixels per point and only within the budget. A frame also takes no more than `MAX_FRAME_PIECES` (16) pieces of the view's canvas (below): each piece is a render and a `drawImage`, their number is the frame's area over the canvas', and a pane dragged almost shut would take hundreds on every render of the GM's (216 pieces no longer held 60 frames a second where 45 did). `playerFrame` gives such a pane a smaller frame of the window's shape, the largest that its pieces hold (`withinPieces`; this comes before the pane's pixels), so the picture stays live with fewer pixels, and `PlayerFrameTexture.copy` brings nothing across of a frame that would take more. *How it is rendered* (`PlayerFrameTexture`, `pixi/`): `PixiRendererOrchestrator.withPlayerSafeFrame` applies the players' layers and the frame's camera (`frameCamera`, centred in the frame's own size) for one render of the stage into a render texture of the frame's size, where the lighting composite reads the scene by copy as in a thumbnail, past the back buffer. One WebGL context cannot draw on a second canvas, so the texture reaches the players' 2D canvas through the view's own: it is drawn there in pieces of the canvas' size, texel on pixel and past the back buffer, and each piece is copied with `drawImage` (`FramePiece`) before the next is drawn; on PIXI's Canvas renderer the texture is a canvas and comes in one piece. Every piece is drawn after a clear of the whole canvas, so nothing of the GM's own picture can show through a texel that is not opaque, and `copy` hands out only the frame `render` has just finished, once (`fresh`): after a render that threw, drew nothing (PIXI skips a stage that is not visible without a word) or lost its context, the texture still holds an earlier frame, of another moment, camera or scene, which must never reach players. Never read the texture back (22 ms of main thread for 3840 × 2160), never resize the renderer or its canvas for a capture (the drawing buffer is allocated twice a frame), and PIXI's `multiView` draws nothing through the back buffer. The frame's size is registered with PIXI's texture pool (`TexturePool.setScreenSize`) so the composite's textures have the frame's size, not the next power of two (25 / 44 MB of textures for 1920 × 1080 / 2560 × 1440), and `release` (the window closed, another scene presented, the view unloaded, a restored context) gives the texture and those back; never clear the pool, which is shared and whose textures the view's filter still holds. *When* (`PlayerFrameMirror`, `services/`): in `RenderScheduler`'s before-render hook (`setBeforeRender`), and the DM's own render that follows in the same task puts the DM's frame back on the canvas the pieces went through, so a mirrored frame costs one extra render of the scene and the DM never sees it; where no render follows (a hidden DM window without a ticker) the DM's frame is rendered again at once. It mirrors at most `PLAYER_MIRROR_FPS` (60) frames a second on any display (slots follow each other, so the remainder of a 75 or 144 Hz frame carries over) and none while the player window is hidden; a skipped frame or a player-visible change without a DM render (`markStale`: settings, freeze, a released hold, a window of another size) makes its loop call `requestRender` once a frame is due, so players never stay on an older state and an idle map is not rendered. Whatever a frame changes must be restored before the DM's render, or the stage keeps rendering. While the source's store has `isMapLoading`, or its graphics context is lost (`canRender`), nothing is rendered for players: a load rewrites the store in steps and the stage holds the scene half built (unlit, without fog or line of sight), which would give the map away. Players keep the last frame (the canvas takes a frame's size only with its first piece), the mirror stays stale, and the first display frame after the load asks for the finished scene. *Frozen*: players frozen on a camera keep the world rectangle it framed (`PlayerCameraState.width` / `height`, pinned by `framedCamera` when they are frozen and saved in the window's session), whatever the pane's size or the GM's camera (in a pane too small for the frame's pieces the same rectangle with fewer pixels); a camera without a rectangle (one an older Atlas saved, or a caller that only knows a camera centred in the GM's screen) frames what the GM's screen shows through it, and a saved one is pinned to that when the window comes back. A freeze without a camera of its own takes the camera of the last frame players were shown of the presented scene (`shownCamera`, forgotten when another scene is presented, as is the session's), else the GM's own, and none while a frame is held or the scene cannot be shown yet (`cameraPlayersSee`): the view's camera is then another scene's, and its rectangle would be shown of this one. The GM is then told that there is nothing to freeze yet (`player.nothingToFreeze`), not that the camera was unfrozen. A frame held while the GM is on another scene tab is a still canvas of the size it was taken with; only it is fitted by CSS (`object-fit: cover`). What players see sized by the GM's zoom (the grid's numbers and when they show, selected token UI, measurement labels, the laser's width, door badges, text) keeps its proportion to the map, as when the picture was a copy. Popouts are closed when the main window unloads, since Obsidian leaves them open across reloads and each one would keep the previous session alive. *The presented scene* (the eye on a scene tab, Send current map to player view) is a fact of its own, not the window's: `presentedSceneOf(app)` (`services/presentedScene.ts`, the tab id and its map file, kept in the vault's local storage since which scene a table shows is this device's) is set by `presentTab` whether or not the window is open, and `presentTab` opens the window on it when players see the scene nowhere: no window open and no plugin showing the presented scene on a screen of its own (`showElsewhere`, which such a plugin calls while it does; the eye, Send current map and the scene switcher all present through it), the window shows it whenever it opens (`openPlayerWindow`, `restorePlayerWindow`, which finds it by tab id, else by file, and prefers it to the scene the window's leaf saved), and others read it through the plugin's `presentedScene` (`get`, `onChange`). `playerWindowStore.shownTabId` is only what an open window shows.
